items.content:
It’s Jackson Hole time!
As he prepares to deliver his first keynote address as Federal Reserve Chair, Kevin Warsh faces a delicate balancing act: how to navigate a remarkably high and varied set of expectations.
On one side are those who want him to follow his predecessors’ tradition of detailing his immediate "reaction function" alongside forward guidance.
On the other are those who hope he returns to the original secular spirit of this unique gathering. This would mean focusing on a growing, complex set of domestic and policy issues at a time of deep structural transformation driven by both technological innovation and geo-economics.
It is a balance that is (i) difficult to strike, (ii) almost certain to leave some unsatisfied, (iii) complicated by non-Fed policy considerations, and yet (iv) bound to tell us a lot about the new Chair.
FWIW, I hope that he tilts more towards the longer-term secular side, especially given the current division among his FOMC colleagues.
 #economy   #markets   #federalreserve   #jacksonhole 
— Mohamed A. El-Erian (@elerianm) Aug 28, 2026

items.title: Good morning. Record currency intervention by Japan: According to Bloomberg reporting, the Japanese Ministry of Finance spent $96 billion in the month ending August 26 to support the yen—a record one-month level augmented by the rare joint and coordinated action with the US on July 31. After strengthening to nearly 156 per dollar immediately following the joint intervention (chart below), the yen has weakened back toward 160, a level widely viewed as a possible trigger line for further intervention. Meanwhile, the big question remains when/if Japan will deploy a more comprehensive policy response involving the Ministry, the Bank of Japan, and the Prime Minister's Office. #economy #markets #y

items.title: The Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge came in as expected this morning: Monthly core PCE inflation for July was 0.2%, and annual was 3.3%, both matching consensus forecasts. Headline ticked up to 0.2% monthly (-0.1% prior and 0.1% expected), leaving the annual figure unchanged at 3.7%. None of this changed market expectations for a September Fed rate hike, which, at around 40%, still feels too high to me. Elsewhere in this morning's data, flat consumer spending reinforces the recent stretch of softer-than-expected economic activity indicators. #economy #markets #federalreserve #inflation

items.title: Secretary Bessent’s remarks just now made it clear that secondary sanctions are central to intensifying US economic pressure on Iran, with "no one above the reach of US sanctions." When reporters pressed on whether China and its entities would be targeted, they were told to wait and see. He noted that the US, using "quiet diplomacy," is making clear to other countries what is expected. He added that he doesn't want to "blow up" the financial system, including asking some "to leave the dollar system," before giving those operating in the "gray areas" time to change. #economy #markets #economicfury #china
